title: Share SSH client config across hosts via agent forwarding
description: home/modules/ssh.nix is now platform-aware and imported through terminal-workstation (neo, trinity) and apoc.nix. Mac uses the 1Password agent and forwards it only to trinity/apoc; Linux hosts use the forwarded SSH_AUTH_SOCK. Verified: Trinity has the Nix-managed config and sees the 1Password keys; Trinity->pve-00 hop authenticates with id_pve_00 (host key checked against Neo trusted fingerprint). Apoc deploy pending: host offline.
notes:
Fixed and verified: ForwardAgent now names the 1Password socket explicitly (bare yes forwards unset SSH_AUTH_SOCK); Linux zsh repoints ~/.ssh/auth-sock at each login's forwarded socket. With 1Password running, a pane with no forwarding and no SSH_AUTH_SOCK sees the keys via the link and hops Trinity->pve-00 with id_pve_00. Earlier failures were 1Password agent refusing connections (app closed/locked). Existing herdr panes need a reconnect plus exec zsh. Apoc not deployed (offline). On branch feat/shared-ssh-config, uncommitted.
Herdr panes lacked the agent because panes and hc exec run under the long-lived herdr-core daemon on Trinity (parent systemd, no SSH_AUTH_SOCK), not under the ssh login. Fix: Linux IdentityAgent and SSH_AUTH_SOCK use stable link ~/.ssh/auth-sock; ~/.ssh/agent-link repoints it at a live forwarded socket, run from ~/.ssh/rc, zsh precmd, and a Match exec in nix-managed.conf. Verified: with the link deliberately dangling and no SSH_AUTH_SOCK, hc exec --on trinity ssh pve-00 healed the link and hopped with id_pve_00.
